title: beta-catenin/TCF4/NANOG axis controls miR-302 transcription in colorectal cancer cells.
authors: Saleki, Kiarash; Xue, Miao; Mazloomi, Amirreza; Spencer-Dene, Bradley; Nateri, Abdolrahman S
one_liner_zh: 该文结合ChIP、报告基因与分子动力学模拟，研究beta-catenin/TCF4与NANOG对miR-302启动子的转录调控及TF-DNA结合互作，虽聚焦癌症转录调控，但TF-DNA结合机制与MD模拟方法对本课题有直接借鉴价值。
abstract: The miR-302 cluster, a key pluripotency-associated non-coding RNA, has been implicated in stem cell homeostasis and tumourigenesis. However, its regulatory mechanisms in cancers, including colorectal cancer (CRC) remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that the beta-catenin/TCF4 complex significantly enhances miR-302 expression through direct promoter activation in CRC cells. We hypothesized that the beta-catenin/TCF4 complex directly activates the miR-302 promoter and cooperates with NANOG in a transcriptional feedback loop sustaining stem-like traits in CRC cells. Using a combination of promoter-driven luciferase reporter assays, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), and molecular dynamics simulations, we identify a regulatory axis involving Wnt signalling and the transcription factor NANOG. Our data show that individual members of the miR-302 cluster activate the NANOG promoter, while both NANOG and beta-catenin/TCF4 synergistically enhance miR-302 promoter activity, suggesting the presence of a positive feedback loop. Structural simulations further elucidate the binding interactions between TCF4, NANOG, and the miR-302 promoter, corroborating our experimental observations. Together, these findings position miR-302 as a downstream effector of Wnt/beta-catenin signalling and an integral component of NANOG-mediated transcriptional networks in CRC stem-like cells. This work advances our understanding of non-coding RNA regulation in cancer and highlights potential therapeutic opportunities for targeting stemness-associated pathways.
abstract_zh: miR-302簇是一种与多能性相关的关键非编码RNA，已被认为在干细胞稳态和肿瘤发生中发挥作用。然而，其在包括结直肠癌（CRC）在内的癌症中的调控机制仍知之甚少。在此，我们证明β-catenin/TCF4复合物通过直接激活启动子显著增强CRC细胞中miR-302的表达。我们假设β-catenin/TCF4复合物直接激活miR-302启动子，并与NANOG在转录反馈环路中协同作用，以维持CRC细胞的干细胞样特性。通过结合启动子驱动的荧光素酶报告基因检测、染色质免疫沉淀（ChIP）和分子动力学模拟，我们识别出一个涉及Wnt信号通路和转录因子NANOG的调控轴。我们的数据显示，miR-302簇的各个成员激活NANOG启动子，而NANOG和β-catenin/TCF4协同增强miR-302启动子活性，提示存在正反馈环路。结构模拟进一步阐明了TCF4、NANOG和miR-302启动子之间的结合相互作用，证实了我们的实验观察结果。综合来看，这些发现将miR-302定位为Wnt/β-catenin信号通路的下游效应因子，以及CRC干细胞样细胞中NANOG介导的转录网络的重要组成部分。这项工作推进了我们对癌症中非编码RNA调控的理解，并强调了靶向干性相关通路的潜在治疗机会。
